text: I push through the wet crowd to the tavern runner and ask him what a bowl of that stew costs, and whether I can eat it somewhere out of this rain.
motivation: He is the person calling out food in the rain. I want a price and a dry place.
intended: Ask the tavern runner the price of a bowl and whether there is shelter to eat it.

text: I nod at the crush of people. If the dry place is inside the market quarter, how do I get through this line, and will the guards let a stranger in just to eat?
motivation: He refused a price and pointed me inside. I need a way through the crowd he named.
intended: Ask the same runner how to reach the market quarter and whether the guards allow entry for a meal.

text: I leave the runner and step up to the nearest gate guard. I ask, plainly, what a traveler has to show or pay to get through this gate.
motivation: The runner told me to ask a gate guard and said they are strict about who passes.
intended: Ask a gate guard the requirement to pass the gate.

text: I keep my eyes on the guard. You are the one watching me right now. What papers, and what fee, are actually in force for a lone traveler at this moment?
motivation: He listed permits, fees, and whoever is watching. I am already speaking to a guard, so I ask him for the current requirement.
intended: Ask this gate guard for the papers and fee required right now.

text: I step away from the guard and go to the notice board he indicated. I read the postings for the taxes, the curfew, and anything that says what a traveler needs in order to pass.
motivation: The guard refused a number and told me the board lists the current taxes, curfew, and passage expectations.
intended: Read the notice board for taxes, curfew, and passage requirements.

text: I leave the board and walk back to the same gate guard. The postings name new taxes and a curfew after dark, but no fee and no papers. Will you let me through tonight, or am I staying outside?
motivation: The board did not state a passage fee or required papers. I take that back to the guard who sent me there and ask for a yes or no.
intended: Ask the same gate guard whether he will let me through tonight.

text: I step into the line and move toward the gate. I tell the guard I have no papers and nothing set aside for a fee, and that I am going through now.
motivation: He said I will not be stopped just for lacking papers or a fee. I try to pass.
intended: Attempt to pass the gate under the condition the guard just stated.

text: I step back out of the line. This guard will not give me a yes or a no. I walk over to the threadbare figure who has been standing still, watching packs and faces, and I ask quietly what they are waiting for.
motivation: The guard keeps refusing to decide. The still figure from the opening is the other person actually present, and they look like they are waiting for something.
intended: Leave the guard and ask the threadbare figure what they are waiting for.

text: I follow their glance. Which crates do you mean, and did you see the patrol there yourself, or is that only what people have been saying?
motivation: They said they are waiting for a sign tied to the missing patrol, and they looked toward crates where it was last seen. I ask whether that is their own sighting.
intended: Ask the threadbare figure which crates they mean and whether they personally saw the patrol.

text: They did not answer me. I leave the threadbare figure and walk up to the gate serjeant who was looking at those crates. I ask him what he is watching for out there.
motivation: The figure stayed silent and the reply put a gate serjeant looking at the crates. I ask that man what he is watching.
intended: Ask the gate serjeant what he is watching toward the crates.
